backtest_protocol.execution_model: Annual receivables are read as raw SEC Companyfacts balance-sheet INSTANT facts (no FY duration) and matched to annual revenue ending the same fiscal-year date; both are known only by filed date (<= signal date). Current DSO uses average current/prior receivables over current revenue, prior DSO uses average prior/pre-prior receivables over prior revenue, and the rule requires DSO to improve year over year. Price confirmation uses only signal-date OHLCV. Paper entry is the next available open with existing entry slippage; exit is the close 10 trading days after the signal with target-side sell slippage and ROUND_TRIP_COST_PCT.
backtest_protocol.source: docs/backtesting.md canonical three-window core replay plus replay-only broad warehouse default-off paper overlay

runtime_fields: raw SEC companyfacts annual receivables instant facts
raw SEC companyfacts annual revenue facts
raw SEC companyfacts filed date and period end

2_history_check.exp-20260528-019: Rejected working-capital discipline (stable receivables/revenue and inventory/revenue as an FGRS support scalar). This run is a standalone candidate-pool source testing receivables DSO/collection trajectory, not a support scalar or inventory/revenue stability.
2_history_check.exp-20260613-031: Rejected operating-efficiency (asset turnover = revenue/assets). This run tests customer-cash collection specifically, not total asset turnover.
2_history_check.exp-20260615-002: Rejected low asset-growth quality. This run tests receivables collection speed rather than broad balance-sheet growth.
2_history_check.exp-20260615-016: Accepted SBC burden improvement is a dilution-quality source. This run tests a separate sales-quality field and does not change SBC thresholds, buyback adjustment, allocator rank, or notional.
2_history_check.exp-20260616-018: Rejected inventory-to-revenue leanness despite strong aggregate EV/PnL because old_thin regressed and drawdown drift was too high. This run exits the inventory family and tests receivables collection quality instead.

pre_run_questions.4_acceptance_standard: Use docs/backtesting.md canonical three windows. Aggregate EV/PnL must be positive, no window EV/PnL regression, at least two EV-improved windows, at least 20 paper trades across all 3 windows, survival >=5%, drawdown drift <=0.5pp, concentration pass, and accepted compression/distribution candidate-pool comparators must be beaten. Replay-only positives are leads until shared daily/backtest parity exists.

prediction.confidence_reason: This uses a materially different free SEC Companyfacts balance-sheet field from the rejected inventory quality scouts and accepted SBC burden source: faster customer cash collection should indicate cleaner sales and lower revenue-quality risk. Prior working-capital support saw missing selected-row coverage, so this is a private data-shape scout with high failure risk; success requires all canonical windows and accepted candidate-pool comparators, not just aggregate PnL.

execution_envelope.failure_handling: missing raw SEC annual receivables instant fact, missing matching FY revenue, missing pre-prior receivables point, stale facts, missing CIK mapping, missing OHLCV, missing next open, or missing 10d exit rejects the paper candidate
execution_envelope.kill_switch: trade_enabled remains false; no production adapter changes
execution_envelope.liquidity_source: price >= $10 and ADV20 >= $50M from PIT OHLCV
execution_envelope.order_semantics: observe-only next-session-open paper entry; no broker order
execution_envelope.portfolio_displacement: none unless a later shared helper and activation gate pass

production_impact.parity_note: This experiment changes no production code. A positive result is only a replay lead until a shared default-off helper computes the same raw SEC receivables instant mapping, filed-date PIT annual revenue facts, DSO/collection improvement gate, liquid SPY-relative confirmation, cooldown, next-open paper entry, 10-day exit, costs, and concentration controls in both historical replay and daily production.
